intro: Picture this: you wake up, open your bungalow door, and a few steps later you're on the walkway along the Prachinburi River, watching the water drift past under a thin morning mist, then you slip into the garden pool before a riverside breakfast — Aroonsawad Riverview Resort is a small riverside resort in Bang Decha sub-district, Mueang Prachinburi district, that sits on a balance that isn't easy to find: quiet by the river yet still about 15 minutes' drive into town · it's a 3-star place done in a green modern-vintage style, with garden bungalows and two-bedroom villas for families · prices start at around THB 1,500/night for a deluxe room · scored 7.2 on Trip.com and 3.6/5 on Tripadvisor from real reviews

body.html: Who Aroonsawad Riverview Resort is for — the shortest way to put it: Aroonsawad Riverview Resort is for people who want a quiet riverside setting but don't want to drive far from Prachinburi town · it isn't a luxe mountain resort like the ones on the Khao Yai side, and it isn't a budget hotel in the middle of town built for a single overnight stay · instead it's a small resort of around 16–19 rooms on the Prachinburi River, in Bang Decha sub-district, Mueang district, that places itself right between rural calm and the convenience of the city · from real reviews on Trip.com and Tripadvisor, the people who say they loved it tend to be couples after a quiet riverside stay, families looking for multi-bedroom villas, and people who like nature and peace and quiet · one foreign review put it plainly, saying the place "suits people who love nature and tranquillity," which sums up its character well · on the flip side, if you're after five-star luxury, or you want to step out of your room and find restaurants and shopping malls right away, this may not be your style, because it sits in a rural riverside zone where you have to drive into town for food and supplies · put another way, it sells quiet and river views first, trading some city-style convenience for them

Location and getting there — what makes Aroonsawad Riverview Resort interesting is a location that's "close but quiet" · the resort sits at 81 Moo 3, Bang Decha sub-district, Mueang Prachinburi district, on the still-rural side of the Prachinburi River · the resort's own information and several booking sites agree it's about 15 min drive, or roughly 6–7 km, from the bus terminal and Prachinburi town · that means you can sleep quietly by the river, but if you're hungry or want to head into town it's a short drive · one thing many people don't realise is that the resort sits right on the river, so you can even arrive by boat if you want — a charm unique to riverside stays · for onward sightseeing, this location reaches Prachinburi's landmarks easily: Wat Kaew Phichit and the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Museum of Thai Traditional Medicine are within about 10 km, and Khao Ito Waterfall is about 13–14 km away · the honest caveat is that you really should have your own car, because it's down a riverside village lane that public transport doesn't reach, and there are no restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance — you mostly drive into town
"A very peaceful place, great for people who love nature and quiet. Lovely riverside atmosphere, the staff are friendly and helpful — you just have to drive into town a bit when you want food."

Room types and decor — Aroonsawad Riverview Resort doesn't have many rooms, around 16–19, which is the upside of a small resort that never feels crowded · they split mainly into two groups · the first is the single-storey deluxe bungalows, set up as semi-detached garden cottages, decorated in a light-green modern-vintage style that blends with the surrounding trees · inside there's air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, a dressing table, a kettle, an en-suite bathroom and Wi-Fi · many rooms have a private balcony or terrace where you can sit and catch the breeze over the garden · the second group is the two-bedroom, two-bathroom villas with a living room, a dining corner and a small kitchen, suited to families or groups of friends travelling together · some villas face the river for full water views, and that's a room worth requesting at the time of booking if the view matters to you · the overall decor leans toward simple and close to nature rather than luxurious · honestly, rooms are where reviews go both ways — some say the rooms are clean and comfortable to sleep in, while others (especially the lower-scoring ones) complain that some rooms are getting old and worn with age, so it's worth checking your room's condition at check-in and taking photos in case you need to ask to switch

Facilities and the pool — for a small resort, Aroonsawad offers facilities that fit a riverside getaway · the highlight is the outdoor pool ringed by trees and garden, a spot guests like to cool off in from the afternoon into the evening · another distinctive feature is the riverside walkway for strolling, soaking up the atmosphere, taking photos, or sitting and watching the water in the morning and evening, which are the prettiest times here · there's also a riverside restaurant, a cafe, free parking, free Wi-Fi throughout, and housekeeping · for anyone looking for an event space, the resort has a meeting room for around 60 people with AV equipment, and it has been used as a riverside wedding venue too · one thing to know is that the front desk isn't open 24 hours like a city hotel — it keeps limited hours, so if you're arriving late you should call ahead · and since it's a riverside garden resort, pets are not allowed

Food and the riverside restaurant — the resort has a riverside restaurant and cafe where you can sit, eat and sip a drink by the water · breakfast is continental, served 7:00 AM–10:00 AM, and some room rates (especially deluxe rooms and villas booked with breakfast) include the morning meal · guests who book a room without breakfast may pay extra for it, so check the conditions clearly when booking · the honest point is that because the resort sits in a rural riverside zone, there are no restaurants within walking distance the way there would be in town, so for food you mainly rely on the resort restaurant, or drive about 15 minutes into town to find somewhere · for anyone planning a multi-day stay who wants to cook for themselves, that's one reason many people choose the villa with a small kitchen · overall the food here is a decent add-on for a getaway, but it isn't a place you come to specifically to eat — plan your meals ahead, or bring some supplies in the car if you're travelling as a group

Service — service is the area that earns fairly consistent praise in real reviews · many reviews, both on Tripadvisor and other booking sites, agree that the staff are friendly, attentive and helpful — even the low-scoring reviews that complain about the rooms still admit the "service is good" · for a small resort run by a small team, having guests feel they're looked after in a friendly way is a real advantage · that said, because it's a small property and the desk isn't open 24 hours, reaching someone at certain times may require a call ahead, especially if you arrive outside operating hours · the resort's contact numbers are 037-287112 and 084-661-2200, and it's worth calling to confirm your booking and ask for directions before you set off, because it sits down a riverside village lane that can be hard to find on a first visit

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling together Trip.com, Tripadvisor and other booking sites, the picture is fairly clear · on the praise side: a quiet riverside setting that's great for relaxing close to nature, a location near town that's still quiet, friendly and helpful staff, a garden pool and riverside walkway that create a nice atmosphere, and multi-bedroom villas that are good value for families · on Tripadvisor it scores about 3.6 out of 5 stars and ranks #7 of 15 specialty lodging properties in Prachinburi, with cleanliness, sleep quality and service rated above 4 stars · on Trip.com the overall score is about 7.2 out of 10 · on the caveat side: the thing brought up most is the distance from town and the inconvenience of finding food around the resort, which is the trade-off for the quiet · on top of that, some low-scoring reviews complain about certain rooms being old and worn, the air conditioning or some fixtures having problems, and the cleanliness of bedding or smells in some bathrooms · these complaints suggest room standards may not be consistent across every unit, so check your room's condition at check-in and don't hesitate to ask to switch if you get one that isn't okay

"The riverside atmosphere is really nice in the morning, you can stroll along the river, and the staff are lovely · but the room I got this time looked a bit old and it's far from town — you have to drive out to find food. Next time I'll ask to see the room before check-in."

Price and value — Aroonsawad Riverview Resort's prices sit in the mid-range for Prachinburi stays · deluxe rooms start at around THB 1,500–1,700/night (sometimes including breakfast) and climb with the season · the two-bedroom villas run around THB 4,200–4,700/night, which is good value once you split it across a group or larger family · compared with budget places in central Prachinburi like Narasiri or Peamsuk Sweet that go for a few hundred baht, Aroonsawad is clearly pricier, but what you get in return is the riverside setting, the pool, and the feel of a garden resort that in-town stays can't offer · on the other hand, compared with similarly priced mountain resorts on the Khao Yai side, some people may feel they'd get mountain views and more facilities there · the bottom line is that the value here depends on how much you prize a "riverside location that's close to town" — if you do, this price is reasonable for a small riverside resort, but choose your room and check the latest reviews before booking to avoid the units whose condition is inconsistent

What to know before you book — a few things make the stay go more smoothly · one, you should have your own car, because the resort is down a riverside village lane that public transport doesn't reach, and there are no restaurants to walk to nearby · two, call to confirm your booking and ask for directions ahead of time at 037-287112 or 084-661-2200, because the spot can be hard to find on a first visit and the desk isn't open 24 hours · three, if you want full river views, request a room or villa facing the river at the time of booking · four, because room standards can be inconsistent, ask to see the room or check its condition at check-in and don't hesitate to ask to switch if you get one that's old or has a smell · five, check whether breakfast is included in the room rate, and plan your meals ahead because you'll rely on the resort restaurant or a drive into town · six, pets aren't allowed here, so if you're bringing one you'll need to find another place

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Aroonsawad Riverview Resort is the best fit for people who want a quiet riverside setting in Prachinburi while staying close enough to town to drive in within about 15 minutes · its strengths are the riverside location, the riverside walkway, the garden pool, the friendly service, and the multi-bedroom villas that are good value for families · what you have to accept is that it's a small rural resort where you need a car, you have to drive into town for food, and room standards aren't consistent across every unit, as some reviews reflect · if you're after five-star luxury, or you want to step out of your room and find restaurants right away, this isn't the answer, and you should look at an in-town hotel like Kantary 304 or a mountain resort on the Khao Yai side instead · but for a slow riverside getaway where you want peace and quiet without a long drive — Aroonsawad Riverview Resort is a riverside option that fits that brief at an accessible price, as long as you pick a good room and set your expectations to match a small riverside resort

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Aroonsawad Riverview Resort Prachinburi

faq.q: Where in Prachinburi is Aroonsawad Riverview Resort, and how do you get there?
faq.a: Aroonsawad Riverview Resort sits at 81 Moo 3, Bang Decha sub-district, Mueang Prachinburi district, on the Prachinburi River · it's about 15 min drive, or roughly 6–7 km, from Prachinburi town and the bus terminal · it's down a riverside village lane that public transport doesn't reach, so you should have your own car and call ahead for directions · it's close to Wat Kaew Phichit, the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Museum and Khao Ito Waterfall

faq.q: How much does Aroonsawad Riverview Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,500/night for a Deluxe garden bungalow · there are deluxe rooms facing the river, and two-bedroom, two-bathroom villas in the range of around THB 4,200–4,700/night, good for families or groups · prices shift with the season and breakfast conditions, so compare a few platforms before booking

faq.q: Does Aroonsawad Riverview Resort have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — there's an outdoor pool in the garden and a riverside restaurant with a cafe · breakfast is continental, served 7:00 AM–10:00 AM, and some room rates include it, so check the conditions when booking · because there are no restaurants to walk to nearby, for food you mainly rely on the resort restaurant or a drive into town

faq.q: Who is Aroonsawad Riverview Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, families and people who love nature and quiet, who want a riverside setting that's still close to town · it has garden bungalows, a pool and a riverside walkway for a slow getaway · but if you're after five-star luxury, or you want to step out of your room and find restaurants right away, this is a small riverside resort focused on quiet, and you'll really need a car

faq.q: What should you know before staying at Aroonsawad Riverview Resort?
faq.a: It's a small 3-star riverside resort · some reviews say room standards are inconsistent, with certain rooms getting old and having air conditioning issues or smells in the bathroom — it's worth asking to see the room or checking its condition at check-in and not hesitating to ask to switch · the front desk isn't open 24 hours, so call ahead at 037-287112 or 084-661-2200 if you arrive outside operating hours · pets aren't allowed here

faq.q: What review scores does Aroonsawad Riverview Resort have?
faq.a: On Trip.com it scores about 7.2 out of 10, and on Tripadvisor about 3.6 out of 5 stars, ranking #7 of 15 specialty lodging properties in Prachinburi · what's praised is the quiet riverside atmosphere and the friendly staff · the main caveats are the distance from town and room standards that aren't consistent across every unit
